title: Personal Credit Cards: how rewards points are earned and clawed back
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: earning rewards points

This calculation guide covers how rewards points are earned on the Personal Credit Cards line, how the quarterly bonus cap works, which transactions never earn, and how a merchant credit takes points back. The rewards program, rates, bonus categories and quarterly cap are the tier's own terms.

## Policy clauses

1. Only tiers whose rewards program is not none earn points.
2. Each posted purchase earns points on its whole-dollar amount; fractions of a dollar are dropped.
3. A purchase whose merchant category is one of the tier's bonus categories earns the tier's bonus rate per dollar while the quarter's bonus-category spending is still below the tier's quarterly cap; the part above the cap earns the tier's base rate.
4. Every other purchase earns the base rate per dollar.
5. Points are rounded down to whole points.
6. Cash advances, balance transfers, fees and interest never earn points.
7. A merchant credit claws back the points its purchase earned, in proportion to the credit, as a points removal linked to that merchant credit.

## The quarter's bonus-category spending

It is the total of the purchases in the tier's bonus categories posted in the calendar quarter that contains this purchase's posted date, counted before this purchase and net of merchant credits on those purchases. On a tier with no quarterly cap, bonus-category purchases always earn the bonus rate.

## Worked examples (hypothetical rates: bonus 4, base 1, quarterly cap 500.00 USD)

| Purchase | Whole dollars | Bonus-category spending before it | Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dining, 80.75 USD | 80 | 450.00 USD | 50 dollars up to the cap at 4, that is 200, plus 30 dollars above it at 1, that is 30: 230 points |
| Grocery, 60.00 USD | 60 | 500.00 USD, cap reached | 60 at 1: 60 points |
| Hardware store, 80.75 USD | 80 | not a bonus category | 80 at 1: 80 points |

With a hypothetical base rate of 1.5, a purchase of 25.60 USD earns on 25 dollars: 25 multiplied by 1.5 is 37.5, rounded down to 37 points.

## Clawback example (hypothetical)

A purchase of 100.00 USD earned 150 points. A merchant credit of 50.00 USD for that purchase is half of it, so 75 points are removed, linked to the merchant credit.

## Points of judgement

- A cash advance of any size earns nothing, even on a tier with a rewards program.
- On a tier whose rewards program is none, no purchase earns points.
